newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CVRD auction might be delayed - minister.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CVRD auction might be delayed - minister.

text.p: The privatization auction of a block of voting shares in Brazilian mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD), scheduled for April 29, might suffer a slight delay, Planning Minister Antonio Kandir said.

Kandir said next Tuesday's sale of a 40-45 percent block of CVRD's voting shares, might be put back by "one, two or three days" because of a host of court cases filed against the privatization of CVRD.
"Clearly we recognize there could be new initiatives," Kandir said, refering to the court cases.

"We would hope to respond to these initiatives as quickly as possible. If there were new problems and our response was not immediate, that could affect the sale by some days. One, two or three days," Kandir said.
The minister then said he expected to see CVRD privatized "by Mothers Day," which in Brazil falls on May 11.
"But it is most likely that the auction will go ahead on April 29," Kandir said.
Until now, government officials have played down speculation the CVRD privatization might have to be postponed due to the sheer number of court cases against it.

The Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF), Brazil's highest court, Wednesday threw out a constitutional challenge against the sale but upheld an injunction which suspended the transfer to CVRD of a large area of the Carajas iron mining region in the Amazon.
At least one other constitutional challenge to the sale has been lodged with the STF although no date has been set for the court to rule on it.
An estimated 60 cases against the CVRD sale have been filed in courts across Brazil.
